app.name: HubSpot (CRM API via HubSpot Developer Platform)

verdict.summary: You can create an OAuth app and install it in your own and test accounts in under an hour, and use it in up to 25 accounts (10 if privately distributed) with no review. Going past 25 accounts requires a manually reviewed HubSpot Marketplace listing. To qualify, the app needs at least 3 unaffiliated production installs, a supported platform version, and only the scopes it actually uses.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to reach a working app; 1-3 days to prepare and submit a Marketplace listing
verdict.approval_wait: None for up to 25 accounts. Marketplace listing: first response within 10 business days, and the full feedback cycle can take up to 60 days.

gates.name: Developer account + developer test accounts
gates.unlocks: Your app can connect to your own HubSpot developer test accounts and to your own standard account.
limits: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes and must be refreshed
The person installing must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission
Unverified apps show a checkbox that the user must tick to confirm authorization before connecting

gates.name: Unlisted marketplace-distribution app / private-distribution app
gates.unlocks: Real customer accounts can install the app without any HubSpot review.
limits: Marketplace-distribution app before listing: up to 25 accounts, not counting developer test accounts
Private-distribution OAuth app: up to 10 allowlisted accounts (up to 100 for Solution Partners)
HubSpot does not grant manual exceptions or temporary increases to these caps (per a community staff reply)
Non-admin users must request access to apps their account admin hasn't approved yet
Rate limit: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account for marketplace apps; 100 (Free/Starter) or 190 (Pro/Enterprise) per 10 seconds for private apps

gates.name: Listed on the HubSpot App Marketplace
gates.unlocks: No install cap: any HubSpot account can install the app.
limits: Only one app can be under review at a time; any other app you submit meanwhile is automatically rejected
Must run on a supported platform version (Projects 2025.1 reached end of support on August 1, 2026)
Classic CRM cards are not allowed; use App Cards
Certification is a separate, optional review: the app must have been listed for 6 months and have 60 or more unaffiliated installs
gates.time_to_reach: Initial review within 10 business days of submission; full cycle up to 60 days after feedback. You need 3 unaffiliated active installs before you can submit.

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Go to developers.hubspot.com and choose the option to create a developer account. You need a developer account to create apps.

steps.title: Scaffold the app project with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI and run `hs project create`. When prompted for distribution, choose marketplace or 'restrict to specific accounts' (private). Choose OAuth as the auth type, not static token. You can start private and switch to marketplace later without losing existing installs.

values.label: Distribution
values.value: Marketplace (25-install cap until listed) or Private (10 allowlisted accounts)

gotchas: Use a supported platform version, 2025.2 or 2026.03. Builds on 2025.1 fail, and apps on unsupported versions are rejected from listing.
Static-token apps are limited to one standard account plus 10 test accounts, and they cannot declare optional scopes.

steps.title: Declare only the scopes you actually use
steps.detail: In the auth block of the app configuration file, list scopes as required, conditionally required, or optional. Start from the Composio default list and remove anything your agent does not call. Move scopes that only some customers need into optional or conditionally required.
gotchas: Scopes you request but don't use fail Marketplace review.
Sensitive contact, company, deal and custom-object scopes, and all custom-object scopes, work only in Enterprise accounts. Users without access to a required scope cannot install the app.
The files and hubdb scopes are legacy; use the granular replacements instead.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's Auth settings, add the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config as the redirect URI.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URL must use https in production; http is allowed only for localhost testing. It must be a domain, not an IP address.
A third-party guide says the match must be exact, including trailing slashes.

steps.title: Upload the project and copy the client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: Upload the project, then open the app's Auth tab and copy the client ID and client secret. Paste them into a custom auth config for the hubspot toolkit in Composio, using the same scopes you declared.
gotchas: Every scope marked required in the app must be in the scope parameter of the authorization URL, or the authorization page shows an error.

steps.title: Create a developer test account and install the app
steps.detail: In your developer account, go to Development > Test accounts and create a test account. Then connect through Composio and approve the install as a Super Admin. Ticking the confirmation checkbox for unverified apps is expected at this stage.

steps.title: Verify the install and token refresh
steps.detail: Go to Development > Monitoring > Logs and open the OAuth tab. Confirm that a TOKEN_EXCHANGE event appears. Then confirm the access token refreshes after its 30-minute lifetime, using grant_type refresh_token.
gotchas: Composio's toolkit metadata lists the token endpoint as /oauth/v1/token, while HubSpot's docs use /oauth/v3/token. If token exchange fails, check which endpoint is being used.

steps.title: Roll out to invited customer accounts
steps.detail: For a private app, add customer accounts to the allowlist under the project's Distribution tab. For an unlisted marketplace app, share the install link. Customer account admins may need to approve the app before non-admin users can connect.
gotchas: The caps are 25 accounts for an unlisted marketplace app and 10 for a private app, with no manual exceptions. Plan for listing if you'll need more.

steps.title: Get at least 3 unaffiliated production installs
steps.detail: Before you can list, the app needs at least three active, unique installs from accounts not affiliated with your organization. Developer test accounts do not count.

steps.title: Prepare the listing materials
steps.detail: Draft live, crawlable Terms and Privacy URLs, a support URL and contact, and an integration-specific setup doc. Also prepare an install button URL, a shared-data table that matches the requested scopes, and accurate pricing. If the app has cards, migrate them to App Cards and keep sensitive scopes out of them.
gotchas: If any required field is missing, the listing stays in Draft mode.
AI connectors must require user-level permissions or be built on HubSpot's MCP server.

steps.title: Record a demo video or guided walkthrough
steps.detail: Since March 31, 2026, HubSpot no longer requires testing credentials with a listing submission and expects a demo video or guided walkthrough instead.

steps.title: Accept the Technology Partner Program agreement and submit the listing
steps.detail: Confirm that OAuth is the app's only auth method and that the public app ID matches the OAuth client ID. Then accept the Technology Partner Program agreement and submit the listing.
gotchas: Submit only one app at a time. HubSpot automatically rejects any other app submitted while one is under review.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing by hand. Expect a first response within 10 business days. The whole cycle should finish within 60 days after HubSpot shares feedback. Once listed, the install cap is removed.

steps.title: (Optional, later) Apply for certification
steps.detail: Once the app has been listed for 6 months and has 60 or more unaffiliated installs, you can apply for certification. This requires a verified domain, a demo video, a security questionnaire, and automatic token refresh with no copy-pasting of codes or tokens. Certification is valid for two years and has no fee.

scopes.effect: HubSpot adds this scope to every app by default.

scopes.scope: crm.objects.contacts.read / crm.objects.contacts.write (and the equivalent companies and deals scopes)
scopes.effect: Standard CRM scopes. Marketplace review requires that the app actually uses every scope it requests.

scopes.scope: crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read (and other sensitive contact, company and deal scopes)
scopes.effect: Work only in Enterprise accounts, and cannot be used in app cards. A third-party guide reports an extra approval step for public apps; HubSpot's docs don't confirm it.
Work only in Enterprise accounts. If you make them required, non-Enterprise customers cannot install, so make them optional or conditionally required.
Legacy scopes. HubSpot recommends migrating to the granular replacements.
HubSpot's scope list doesn't mark these as legacy, though third-party guides do. Request them only if you use them.

blockers.symptom: New installs are blocked after 25 accounts (or 10 for a private app)
blockers.cause: HubSpot caps installs for unlisted apps and does not grant exceptions.
blockers.fix: Get the app listed on the Marketplace, or plan your rollout around the cap.

blockers.symptom: The authorization page shows an error
blockers.cause: A scope marked required in the app is missing from the scope parameter of the authorization URL.
blockers.fix: Make the Composio auth config scopes match the app's required scopes exactly.

blockers.cause: A required scope is not available in their account tier (for example, Enterprise-only custom-object or sensitive scopes), or the user is not a Super Admin or Marketplace Access user.
blockers.fix: Move tier-specific scopes to optional or conditionally required, and have an admin do the install.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or left in Draft mode
blockers.cause: Unused scopes, missing listing fields, fewer than 3 unaffiliated installs, or an unsupported platform version.
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes, fill in every required listing field, and move the project to 2025.2 or 2026.03.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected because of CRM cards
blockers.cause: Classic CRM cards sunset on October 31, 2026 and are not allowed in new listings.
blockers.fix: Migrate to App Cards on Projects 2025.2 or 2026.03.

blockers.symptom: Your second app submission is rejected automatically
blockers.cause: HubSpot reviews only one app per developer at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the first app's review to finish before submitting another.

blockers.cause: Marketplace apps are limited to 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account, and the API limit add-on doesn't raise this. Private apps get 100 or 190 per 10 seconds depending on tier.
blockers.fix: Add backoff and batch requests in the agent.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app (OAuth2, or the API key option) to prototype. Register your own app when you need your own branding, client ID or redirect domain, or a Marketplace listing. Your own app is capped at 25 accounts (unlisted marketplace) or 10 accounts (private) until it is listed. Composio's default scope list is long and includes custom-object scopes that only work in Enterprise accounts, so trim it to what your agent uses before creating your own app.

open_questions: Refresh-token lifetime and expiry rules were not found in HubSpot's docs.
PKCE support was not confirmed either way.
Composio's toolkit lists the token endpoint as /oauth/v1/token but HubSpot's docs use /oauth/v3/token. It is unclear which one Composio actually calls with a custom app.
Unknown whether Composio's managed HubSpot app is subject to the 25-install or 10-account cap, or to its own limits.
HubSpot's docs do not confirm whether public apps need a separate review for sensitive scopes beyond the app-card rule.
Unresolved whether tickets and timeline are legacy scopes.
Whether apps can be created in the web UI without the CLI was not verified.
Per-account rate limits for marketplace apps conflict: 110 per 10 seconds in the usage guidelines vs 100 on the certification page.
The install and review flow was not tested end to end; it is based on HubSpot's documentation.
